body.translated_text:
<s>Sudhanakinnaryavadāna</s> (The Story of <s>Sudhana</s> and the <s>Kinnarī</s>)
from: <s>Kṣemendra</s>: <s>Avadānakalpalatā</s> (<s>Avadāna</s> 64) = KAvk_64

children.translated_text: Even for those whose minds are tender as fresh sprouts, yet whose fortitude is hard as a thunderbolt,

children.text: mahatāṃ maṇivimalānāṃ api bhavati na rāgasaṃkrāntiḥ // KAvk_64.1 //
children.translated_text: for the great ones, pure as jewels, there is no transference of passion. // KAvk_64.1 //

body.text: śākyālaye darśanam eva pitrā sarvānukampī bhṛśam arthyamānaḥ

children.text: yadā yadānandasudhārasendur viveśa śāstā nijarājadhānīṃ // KAvk_64.2 //
children.translated_text: whenever that moon of bliss-nectar, the <s>Śāstā</s> (Teacher), entered his own royal capital — // KAvk_64.2 //

body.translated_text: Earnestly entreated by his father for even a glimpse at the <s>Śākya</s> palace, the all-compassionate one,

children.translated_text: then each time, the doe-eyed <s>Yaśodharā</s>, standing atop the palace, making the beauty of her eyes an ornament for her ears,

children.text: kāntyā diśāṃ vismayam ullikhantaṃ yaśodharā taṃ dayitaṃ vilokya // KAvk_64.3 //
children.translated_text: beholding that beloved one whose splendor inscribed wonder upon the directions — // KAvk_64.3 //
hopeless of union and embrace with him, her every hope bewildered, as if poisoned by anguish,

children.text: dhṛtiṃ vayasyām iva vārayantīṃ nirasya saudhāt tanum utsasarja // KAvk_64.4 //
children.translated_text: pushing away her composure as if it were a friend trying to restrain her, she cast herself down from the palace roof. // KAvk_64.4 //

children.text: yadā yadā pallavapeśalāṅgī dehaṃ samutsṛṣṭavatī satī sā /
children.translated_text: Whenever that virtuous woman with limbs delicate as tender shoots flung her body down,

children.text: tadā tadā manmathamohitāṃ tāṃ dayārdracakṣur bhagavān rarakṣa // KAvk_64.5 //
children.translated_text: each time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), with eyes moist with compassion, protected her who was deluded by the god of love. // KAvk_64.5 //

children.text: tataḥ kadā cid bhagavān vanānte tatkautukād bhikṣugaṇena pṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then once, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in a forest grove, questioned by the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) out of curiosity about this,

children.text: jagāda dantadyuticandrikābhir nivārayan rāgam ivādharasya // KAvk_64.6 //
children.translated_text: spoke, as if dispelling the passion of his lower lip with the moonbeams of his teeth's radiance — // KAvk_64.6 //

children.text: yaśodharā madviraheṇa nityaṃ karoti yat sāhasam etad ārtā /
children.translated_text: "That <s>Yaśodharā</s>, tormented by separation from me, constantly commits this reckless act —

children.text: haranti dhairyaṃ vitaranti mohaṃ eṣa svabhāvaḥ smaravibhramāṇāṃ // KAvk_64.7 //
children.translated_text: they steal away composure and spread delusion; such is the nature of love's bewilderments. // KAvk_64.7 //

children.text: mayāpi tasyā viraheṇa pūrvaṃ janmāntare māravimohitena /
children.translated_text: I too, in a former birth, deluded by <s>Māra</s>, by separation from her,
endured great sorrow that became the cause of clinging anguish, attended by abundant calamity. // KAvk_64.8 //
Long ago, in the excellent city of <s>Hastināpura</s>, a city that had conquered the city of the gods,
there was a king named <s>Dhana</s>, a treasury of virtues and prosperity. // KAvk_64.9 //
He embraced the earth with his arm, placed <s>Sarasvatī</s> (learning) at his throat,

children.text: lakṣmīḥ prasādhitā yena kīrtir eva pravāsitā // KAvk_64.10 //
children.translated_text: adorned <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity), and sent forth <s>Kīrti</s> (fame) alone to travel abroad. // KAvk_64.10 //
From his lovely wife <s>Rāmā</s>, a son named <s>Sudhana</s>
was born, famed as if a hundred treasures had arisen together with him. // KAvk_64.11 //
Ever delighting in the blossoming of all arts like a night-lily garden,

children.text: kalāvān nirmalarucir yaḥ pūrṇendur ivābabhau // KAvk_64.12 //
children.translated_text: skilled in the arts, of spotless radiance, he shone like the full moon. // KAvk_64.12 //
That earth-lord had a neighboring king,
a proud one named <s>Mahendrasena</s>, renowned for his great valor. // KAvk_64.13 //
By him, whose punishment was unbearable, who seized everyone's entire possessions,
who was like untimely Death itself, the subjects were oppressed and grieved. // KAvk_64.14 //
As that king pursued <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), with all celebration of merit ceased,

children.text: tīvropatāpasaṃtapte pure na vavṛṣur ghanāḥ // KAvk_64.15 //
children.translated_text: in his city, scorched by fierce affliction, the clouds did not rain. // KAvk_64.15 //
With the king hostile, there arose in that land a catastrophic famine —

children.text: babhūva vyasaneṣv eva bhavanti vyasanodayāḥ // KAvk_64.16 //
children.translated_text: for calamities indeed arise amidst calamities. // KAvk_64.16 //
Then all the city-dwellers, afflicted by extreme distress,
agitated by the misfortunes of the wicked ruler, gathered together and deliberated: // KAvk_64.17 //
"By this king, a moon of faults, this dull-witted populace has been utterly
shut down like a lotus pond by the fresh fall of frost. // KAvk_64.18 //
This one, always addicted to vices, approved by dishonest ministers,
squeezes us dry and nourishes his jesters, servants, and singers. // KAvk_64.19 //
Grievous too is the drought, born from the curse of this sinful king's evil,
producing famine, bearing witness to the destruction of the people. // KAvk_64.20 //
The king is exceedingly harsh; his retinue are rough, noisy fools;
his ministers are miserly, skilled in bitter fraud and crookedness;
the officials in their posts are enraged, afflicted with the disease of hostile looks —

children.text: kathaṃ sahyaḥ so 'yaṃ kṛpaṇadalano dāruṇagaṇaḥ // KAvk_64.21 //
children.translated_text: how can this cruel gang that crushes the poor be endured? // KAvk_64.21 //
King <s>Dhana</s>, illustrious, is heard to be one who increases his kingdom;

children.text: gacchāmas tatpuraṃ so 'smān vatsalaḥ pālayiṣyati // KAvk_64.22 //
children.translated_text: let us go to his city — that compassionate one will protect us. // KAvk_64.22 //

children.text: apatyam iva rāṣṭraṃ yaḥ sadā paśyati bhūpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: A king who always regards his realm as his own child —

children.text: viṣaye jīvyate tasya janakasyeva veśmani // KAvk_64.23 //
children.translated_text: one lives in his domain as in a father's house." // KAvk_64.23 //

children.text: iti niścayam ādhāya yayus te hastināpuraṃ /
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, they departed for <s>Hastināpura</s> —

children.text: tyājyaḥ kāyo 'pi sāpāyaḥ kiṃ punar deśasaṃśrayaḥ // KAvk_64.24 //
children.translated_text: even a body fraught with danger should be abandoned, how much more a mere dwelling place! // KAvk_64.24 //
Learning that his own city had become deserted, King <s>Mahendrasena</s>,
filled with intense remorse, angrily addressed his chief ministers: // KAvk_64.25 //
"Our spies, those who move in secret, have reported to us

children.text: prayātā iti naś cāraiḥ kathitaṃ gūḍhacāribhiḥ // KAvk_64.26 //
children.translated_text: that the residents of my city have gone to the city of the wealthy King <s>Dhana</s>. // KAvk_64.26 //

children.text: durbhikṣakhinnā yadi te yātā mama ripoḥ puram /
children.translated_text: If they, afflicted by famine, have gone to my enemy's city,

children.text: tat sarvatra bhavanty eva paryāyair devaviplavāḥ // KAvk_64.27 //
children.translated_text: well, divine calamities occur everywhere in turn. // KAvk_64.27 //

children.text: atha vā rājadoṣena gatās te sukhavāñchayā /
children.translated_text: Or perhaps they have gone due to the king's faults, desiring happiness —

children.text: viṣṭidaṇḍakaronmuktaḥ kasya rājñaḥ pure janaḥ // KAvk_64.28 //
children.translated_text: in what king's city are the people free from forced labor, punitive taxes, and levies? // KAvk_64.28 //
Generally, out of contempt for the familiar, people always seek the new;

children.text: dūrastha eva sarvasya sarvo bhavati vallabhaḥ // KAvk_64.29 //
children.translated_text: everyone who is distant is always dear to everyone. // KAvk_64.29 //
What quality of that king is superior to ours,

children.text: pareṣāṃ harate yena mugdhā jāyā iva prajāḥ // KAvk_64.30 //
children.translated_text: by which he steals away our naive subjects like a wife? // KAvk_64.30 //
Let a stratagem be devised to quell his pride;

children.text: samṛddhikāraṇaṃ yac ca tadvighāto vidhīyatāṃ // KAvk_64.31 //
children.translated_text: and whatever is the cause of his prosperity — let its destruction be contrived!" // KAvk_64.31 //
Hearing the king's words, the chief ministers spoke:

children.text: śrūyatāṃ deva yenāsau rājā dhanajanorjitaḥ // KAvk_64.32 //
children.translated_text: "Hear, O lord, the reason why that King <s>Dhana</s> is thriving with people and prosperity: // KAvk_64.32 //
In his realm there is a <s>Nāgarāja</s> (serpent king) named <s>Citra</s>, of abundant waters,

children.text: tasya kṣitipater mūrtaḥ puṇyabaddha ivodayaḥ // KAvk_64.33 //
children.translated_text: who is like the embodied fortune of that king, bound by his merit. // KAvk_64.33 //
By his power, crops ripen even out of season,
and all the prosperities of kings are rooted in agricultural abundance. // KAvk_64.34 //

children.text: tasmād vidyābalān nāgaḥ sa hartuṃ yadi śakyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, if that <s>Nāga</s> can be seized by the power of <s>vidyā</s> (magic spells),

children.text: tadā yānti svayaṃ tasya prajās tvām eva saṃśrayam // KAvk_64.35 //
children.translated_text: then his subjects will come of their own accord to you for refuge. // KAvk_64.35 //

children.text: dīptamantrabalaṃ kaṃ cit tasmād anviṣya sādhakam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, by seeking out some practitioner possessed of powerful blazing <s>mantras</s>,

children.text: nāgarājasya haraṇe kriyatāṃ tūrṇam udyamaḥ // KAvk_64.36 //
children.translated_text: let effort be made swiftly for the capture of the <s>Nāgarāja</s>." // KAvk_64.36 //

children.text: ity amātyavacaḥ śrutvā tathety āha mahīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing the ministers' words, the king said "So be it" —
the wicked, incapable of cultivating their own virtues, are eager to attack others' merits. // KAvk_64.37 //
Then, having proclaimed a reward of abundant gold,

children.text: kṛtvā te mantriṇaḥ prāpur nāgabandhanamantriṇam // KAvk_64.38 //
children.translated_text: those ministers found a sorcerer skilled in <s>nāga</s>-binding <s>mantras</s>. // KAvk_64.38 //
That one, named <s>Vidyādhara</s>, engaged by them with the promise of gold,

children.text: prārthitaś citram ānetuṃ prayayau hastināpuram // KAvk_64.39 //
children.translated_text: set out for <s>Hastināpura</s> to bring <s>Citra</s>. // KAvk_64.39 //
There, at the forest's edge, amid trees of lush dark foliage,

children.text: bhavanaṃ bhogināṃ bhartuḥ sa dadarśa nabhaḥprabham // KAvk_64.40 //
children.translated_text: he beheld the abode of the lord of serpents, radiant as the sky — // KAvk_64.40 //
with flourishing garlands of <s>bakula</s> flowers, with the splendor of a gleaming <s>tilaka</s> mark,
like a jeweled mirror serving as an ornament near the goddess of the forest. // KAvk_64.41 //
Seeing that place with its crystal-clear waters, his mind stained with greed,
he girded himself with the concentration of <s>mantras</s> and performed the <s>digbandha</s> (binding of the directions) for success. // KAvk_64.42 //
When the <s>digbandha</s> was performed by him, of terribly fierce power through his vow,
a headache arose in the <s>Nāgapati</s> (lord of serpents), whose hood-jewel burned. // KAvk_64.43 //
Then, rising up invisibly and seeing that <s>mantra</s>-practitioner,
the <s>Phaṇipati</s> (lord of hooded serpents), trembling with fear of capture, reflected: // KAvk_64.44 //
"With tawny brows and beard, streaked with grey, with lightning-yellow eyes,
resembling untimely Death — he has come to destroy my family. // KAvk_64.45 //
Now this evil-souled one has performed a <s>digbandha</s> in the forest;

children.text: badhnāty eṣa na yāvan māṃ tāvad yuktikramaḥ kṣamaḥ // KAvk_64.46 //
children.translated_text: before he binds me, a tactical course of action is fitting. // KAvk_64.46 //
On the bank nearby dwells the great sage <s>Valkalāyana</s>;

children.text: jāne so 'pi na me sādhu paritrāṇe pragalbhate // KAvk_64.47 //
children.translated_text: I know that even he would not dare to protect me. // KAvk_64.47 //
But the one who is always devoted to serving him at his hermitage,

children.text: lubdhakaḥ padmako nāma sa me saṃrakṣaṇakṣamaḥ // KAvk_64.48 //
children.translated_text: the hunter named <s>Padmaka</s> — he is capable of protecting me." // KAvk_64.48 //

children.text: iti niścitya manasā sa gatvā lubdhakāntikam /
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved in his mind, he went to the hunter
and, revealing his situation, begged him for protection from capture. // KAvk_64.49 //
Entreated by the <s>Nāgarāja</s> to slay the practitioner,

children.text: dhanvī taṃ deśam abhyetya mantradhīraṃ vyalokayat // KAvk_64.50 //
children.translated_text: that bowman approached the spot and observed the one steadfast in <s>mantras</s>. // KAvk_64.50 //
At that very moment, the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner, having offered oblations to the fire,
performed the invocation of the <s>Nāgarāja</s>, eager for his capture. // KAvk_64.51 //

body.text:
mantrākṛṣṭe phaṇipatau kṣaṇaṃ tadbhavanodakam /
saviṣādaṃ rurodeva prodyadbudbudagadgadam // KAvk_64.52 // saṃtrāsavihvalabhujaṅgavadhūviṣādaniśvāsavegavihitojjvalaphenamālam /

children.text: rakṣārthanām iva cakāra taraṅgahastasaktāñjali prabalakampavilolam ambhaḥ // KAvk_64.53 //
children.translated_text: The water, with its wave-hands pressing together in agitation, as if for the purpose of protection, trembled violently with powerful quaking. // KAvk_64.53 //

body.translated_text:
When the <s>Phaṇipati</s> was drawn by the <s>mantras</s>, the waters of his abode for a moment
wept as it were in sorrow, stammering with rising bubbles. // KAvk_64.52 // Adorned with brilliant garlands of foam produced by the force of the anguished sighs of the serpent-wives, distraught with terror,

children.translated_text: When that <s>nāga</s> was seized by him through the power of his <s>vidyā</s> (magical knowledge), [the nāga] having the brilliance of <s>Garuḍa</s>,
and the water-vessel was cast aside with its coils contracted and curled — // KAvk_64.54 //
that gold-greedy one, with eyes trembling in fear,

children.text: vivyādha dhanur ākṛṣya viṣadigdhena lubdhakaḥ // KAvk_64.55 //
children.translated_text: was pierced by the hunter, drawing his bow, with a poison-smeared arrow. // KAvk_64.55 //
Approaching that one into whom the arrow had sunk, who had further abandoned the serpent,
he beheaded him with a terrible sword. // KAvk_64.56 //
That <s>vidyā</s> (magical knowledge), like a harlot, out of greed served another;

children.text: abhūt siddhāpi mugdhasya svavināśāya kevalam // KAvk_64.57 //
children.translated_text: though perfected, she became, for the deluded one, the cause of his own destruction alone. // KAvk_64.57 //
The powers of <s>vidyā</s> and wealth, employed for the torment of others,
suddenly perish for the utterly deluded, along with their very lives. // KAvk_64.58 //
Then, filled with great joy, the grateful lord of serpents,

children.text: taṃ nināya svabhavanaṃ lubdhakaṃ snehalubdhadhīḥ // KAvk_64.59 //
children.translated_text: his mind seized by affection, led that hunter to his own abode. // KAvk_64.59 //
There, in jeweled mansions amid gardens of gem-studded creepers and aerial palaces,

children.text: abhyarcyamānaś citreṇa kaṃ cit kālam uvāsa saḥ // KAvk_64.60 //
children.translated_text: honored in wondrous fashion, he dwelt for some time. // KAvk_64.60 //

children.text: kadā cid atha nāgena pūjyamānaṃ savismayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then once, while being worshipped by the <s>nāga</s>, he beheld with astonishment

children.text: vidyuddāmopamaṃ pāśam amoghākhyaṃ dadarśa saḥ // KAvk_64.61 //
children.translated_text: an infallible noose called <s>Amogha</s>, resembling a streak of lightning. // KAvk_64.61 //

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā tatprabhāvaṃ ca śrutvā nāganiveditam /
children.translated_text: Having seen it and heard of its power as told by the <s>nāga</s>,

children.text: yatnāt tadarthanāṃ cakre lubdhako lubdhamānasaḥ // KAvk_64.62 //
children.translated_text: the hunter, his mind overcome with greed, earnestly sought to obtain it. // KAvk_64.62 //
Unconquerable in the exertion of battle, a fetter even of the gods —

children.text: taṃ jīvitādhikaṃ tasmai dadau prītyā phaṇīśvaraḥ // KAvk_64.63 //
children.translated_text: that [noose], dearer than his own life, the lord of serpents gave to him with affection. // KAvk_64.63 //

children.text: tatas taṃ pāśam ādāya citram āmantrya lubdhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, taking that noose, the hunter bid farewell to <s>Citra</s> (the nāga),

children.text: uttīrya nāgabhavanāl labdhārthaḥ svapadaṃ yayau // KAvk_64.64 //
children.translated_text: and ascending from the <s>nāga</s> realm, having obtained his goal, he went to his own place. // KAvk_64.64 //
Having long enjoyed the wealth obtained through the <s>nāga</s>'s power,
he gave the noose to his son named <s>Utpalaka</s> and passed away. // KAvk_64.65 //
Following his father's conduct, that hunter's son too,
by the tradition of his family, became devoted to the service of that sage. // KAvk_64.66 //

body.text:
tataḥ kadā cit sa muner viśrāntasya sthitaḥ puraḥ /
śuśrāva kākalīgītaṃ kīrṇaṃ karṇarasāyanam // KAvk_64.67 // gītaśravaṇaniṣpandanilīnahariṇaṃ vanam /
citranyastam ivālokya so 'pṛcchad vismito munim // KAvk_64.68 // kamalābandhasaṃruddhamadhupadhvanisodaraḥ /

children.translated_text: 'Whence is this sound heard, as sweet as the cooing of a cuckoo?' // KAvk_64.69 //

body.translated_text: Then once, standing before the resting sage, he heard a melodious song (<s>kākalīgīta</s>) poured forth, a nectar to the ears. // KAvk_64.67 // The forest, with its deer motionless from listening to the song, appeared as if painted in a picture; seeing this, he asked the sage in wonder —

children.text: iti lubdhakaputreṇa pṛṣṭas taṃ munir abravīt /
children.translated_text: Thus asked by the hunter's son, the sage said to him:
'<s>Kinnarī</s> maidens sing this sweet melody. // KAvk_64.70 //
The daughter of <s>Druma</s>, the king of <s>Kinnaras</s>, surrounded by hundreds of maidens,

children.text: pañcabhir nāgabhavane krīḍaty eṣā manoharā // KAvk_64.71 //
children.translated_text: these five enchanting ones sport in the <s>nāga</s> realm.' // KAvk_64.71 //

children.text: śrutvaitat kautukākrāntaḥ sa punar munim abhyadhāt /
children.translated_text: Hearing this, seized with curiosity, he again addressed the sage:

children.text: api śaknoti puruṣaḥ prāptuṃ kinnarakanyakām // KAvk_64.72 //
children.translated_text: 'Is a man able to obtain a <s>kinnarī</s> maiden?' // KAvk_64.72 //

children.text: tam uvāca munir yasya bhavet pāśaḥ karāgragaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sage said to him: 'He who has in hand the noose

children.text: amoghākhyaḥ sa śaknoti hartuṃ kinnarakāminīm // KAvk_64.73 //
children.translated_text: called <s>Amogha</s> — he is able to capture a <s>kinnarī</s> beloved.' // KAvk_64.73 //

children.text: etad ākarṇya sotsāhas taṃ praṇamyātha lubdhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing this, filled with enthusiasm, that hunter, having bowed to him,
set forth taking the noose, toward the vicinity of the lord of serpents' abode. // KAvk_64.74 //
There, he saw the troupe of <s>kinnarīs</s>, marked by playful dalliance,
bearing the beauty of a golden creeper-grove swaying in the wind. // KAvk_64.75 //

children.text: madbye snānotthitāṃ tāsāṃ sa dadarśa manoharām /
children.translated_text: In their midst, he beheld one who had risen from bathing — the enchanting <s>Manoharā</s>,
like the water-goddess who extinguishes the fire of <s>Smara</s>'s (Love's) third eye. // KAvk_64.76 //

body.text:
anaṅgavibhramārambhanirbharormiṇi yauvane /
majjataḥ śaiśavasyeva kurvāṇām avalambanam // KAvk_64.77 // mekhalābaddhasaṃnaddhadivyāmbaramanoramām /

children.translated_text: like a row of abundant foam clinging to the art of water-sport — // KAvk_64.78 //

body.translated_text: In her youth — an ocean overflowing with mighty waves of Love's playful agitation — as if providing a support for childhood that was sinking therein, // KAvk_64.77 // charming with divine garments tightly bound by her girdle,

children.translated_text: As if by a great flowing stream of loveliness,
she was stealing the beauty of the moon-white night with her string of pearls. // KAvk_64.79 //
Redrawing the ornamental leaf-design (<s>pattralatā</s>) on her cheeks that had been washed by the water,
with the cluster of rays from the gems of her earrings — // KAvk_64.80 //
A <s>tilaka</s> mark was being drawn on her forehead by her friend with a line of musk,
as if dispelling the moon's impotence in [the art of] producing a blemish-mark. // KAvk_64.81 //
Seeing her, his mind drawn by the noose of wonder's possession,

children.text: cakre pāśam amoghākhyaṃ sajjaṃ sapadi lubdhakaḥ // KAvk_64.82 //
children.translated_text: the hunter immediately readied the noose called <s>Amogha</s>. // KAvk_64.82 //
Then, trembling with sudden terror, the doe-eyed

children.text: kinnaryo divam utpetuḥ pāśahastaṃ vilokya taṃ // KAvk_64.83 //
children.translated_text: <s>kinnarīs</s> flew up to the sky, seeing him with the noose in hand. // KAvk_64.83 //
With nimble hand casting the noose, he captured the startled-eyed

children.text: manoharāṃ sa jagrāha hariṇīm iva lubdhakaḥ // KAvk_64.84 //
children.translated_text: <s>Manoharā</s>, just as a hunter [captures] a doe. // KAvk_64.84 //

children.text: sā pāśavivaśā tena kṛṣṭā kaṣṭadaśāṃ śritā /
children.translated_text: She, overpowered by the noose, dragged by him, reduced to a wretched state,

children.text: kim etad iti nājñāsīt kṣaṇamūrcchānimīlitā // KAvk_64.85 //
children.translated_text: did not know 'What is this?' — her eyes closed in a momentary swoon. // KAvk_64.85 //
Like a doe separated from her herd, with the hope of seeing her own kin,

children.text: nirīkṣamāṇā kakubhaḥ sā saṃbhrāntā tam abhyadhāt // KAvk_64.86 //
children.translated_text: gazing at the quarters in distress, she said to him: // KAvk_64.86 //

children.text: muñca muñca dṛḍhākṣiptāṃ mā sprākṣīḥ parirakṣa mām /
children.translated_text: 'Release me! Release me, firmly bound! Do not touch me — protect me!

children.text: krūrā api bhavanty eva śokārtiṣu kṛpālavaḥ // KAvk_64.87 //
children.translated_text: Even the cruel become compassionate toward those in the agony of grief!' // KAvk_64.87 //
'A divine maiden, employed through greed for the highest station,

children.text: sadyaḥ pradīptā vidyeva nirdahaty eva sādhakam // KAvk_64.88 //
children.translated_text: like a <s>vidyā</s> (spell) suddenly blazing, burns the practitioner himself. // KAvk_64.88 //

children.text: māṃ vicārya dhiyā dhīmann ucitāya prayacchataḥ /
children.translated_text: If you wisely consider me and bestow me upon a worthy one,
there will surely come to you a great acquisition of merit and wealth! // KAvk_64.89 //

children.text: pīḍāṃ pāśakṛtām etāṃ na sahe muñca bandhanam /
children.translated_text: I cannot endure this pain inflicted by the noose — release these bonds!

children.text: svayaṃ vrajāmy ahaṃ tatra yatra te 'bhimatā gatiḥ // KAvk_64.90 //
children.translated_text: I shall go of my own will to wherever your desired destination may be.' // KAvk_64.90 //

children.text: divam utplutya gacchāmi na tv ahaṃ muktabandhanā /
children.translated_text: 'I fly up and travel through the sky — but not when freed from bonds;

children.text: yadvaśān me gatir vyomni cūḍāratnaṃ gṛhāṇa tat // KAvk_64.91 //
children.translated_text: that by whose power my path lies through the sky — take that crest-jewel!' // KAvk_64.91 //

children.text: ity uktaḥ sa tayā sāsraṃ prayātaḥ karuṇārdratām /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by her with tears, he was moved to compassion;

children.text: cūḍāmaṇiṃ samādāya pāśaṃ muktvā jagāda tām // KAvk_64.92 //
children.translated_text: taking the crest-jewel and releasing the noose, he said to her: // KAvk_64.92 //

children.text: samāśvasihi kalyāṇi na śokaṃ kartum arhasi /
children.translated_text: 'Be comforted, O auspicious one! You should not grieve.

children.text: na nāmānucitāya tvāṃ prayacchāmi nijecchayā // KAvk_64.93 //
children.translated_text: I shall not, of my own desire, give you to anyone unworthy. // KAvk_64.93 //
There is a glorious prince, a great ocean of jewel-like virtues,

children.text: pūritāḥ kakubhaḥ sarvā yena kīrtyamṛtormibhiḥ // KAvk_64.94 //
children.translated_text: by whom all the quarters have been filled with waves of the nectar of fame. // KAvk_64.94 //
He is a mirror for the face of learning, an ornament of the play of arts,
well-conducted, named <s>Sudhana</s>, the distinction of his own lineage. // KAvk_64.95 //

body.text:
sa te samucitaḥ subhru vibhramābharaṇaṃ bhuvaḥ /
tyāgopabhogasubhagaḥ sukhotsava iva śriyaḥ // KAvk_64.96 // surakinnaragandharvavidyādharavilāsinām /

children.translated_text: the lord of the earth who is the lord of the [night of the] new moon. // KAvk_64.97 //

body.translated_text: He is worthy of you, O fair-browed one, an ornament of grace for the earth, fortunate in generosity and enjoyment, like a joyous festival for <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune). // KAvk_64.96 // He humbles the pride of the courtesans of gods, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and <s>vidyādharas</s> —

children.translated_text: Thus consoled by him, separated from her kinfolk,
<s>Manoharā</s> lamented most piteously, like an osprey. // KAvk_64.98 //
Meanwhile, <s>Sudhana</s>, curious for the sport of hunting on the slopes of the <s>Vindhya</s>,

children.text: prasthitaḥ sudhano dhanvī śanais taṃ deśam āyayau // KAvk_64.99 //
children.translated_text: set forth with his bow and gradually arrived at that region. // KAvk_64.99 //
From the sound of his chariot-wheels, the circle of peacocks began to dance,
and the beauty of the forest momentarily assumed the appearance of a swaying dark-blue silken garment. // KAvk_64.100 //
He shone with drops of perspiration on his cheeks,
as if with beautiful pearls that had migrated to the edge of his earrings. // KAvk_64.101 //
The dust raised by the hooves of his chariot-horses, [appearing to be] gathered before him by the rays of his teeth,

children.text: harann iva rajaḥpuñjaṃ vyājahāra sa sārathim // KAvk_64.102 //
children.translated_text: as if drawing in [the dust], he spoke to his charioteer: // KAvk_64.102 //
'Ah! As if by a chariot of the mind, by this wind-swift chariot,

children.text: dūrojjhitā svasainyena kiyatī laṅghitā kṣitiḥ // KAvk_64.103 //
children.translated_text: how much land has been traversed, leaving my army far behind! // KAvk_64.103 //
These <s>pippala</s> (sacred fig) leaves, trembling with the sport of the gentle breeze,
steal the green hue of the earth adorned with deer. // KAvk_64.104 //
These [vines], with lips of young shoots and bosoms swelling with flower-clusters,

children.text: sotkaṇṭhā iva jṛmbhante mañjaryaḥ śvasanākulāḥ // KAvk_64.105 //
children.translated_text: yawn as if with longing, their blossoms agitated by the breeze. // KAvk_64.105 //
These rows of forest trees, clad in mantles of emerald-dark grass,
shine resplendent, tinted with the pollen of flowers. // KAvk_64.106 //
These deer, their necks turned back, fleeing in alarm,
seem to scatter groves of blue lotuses with their darting glances. // KAvk_64.107 //
These young elephants, with tusks lovely as moonbeam-shoots, with temples equal to the breasts of the beloved of the village-chief,

children.text: paśyanti dantiśiśavaḥ parito rathaṃ me nemisvanāpaḥrtacāpalalīnakarṇāḥ // KAvk_64.108 //
children.translated_text: gaze all around at my chariot, their ears flattened and hidden by the sound of the wheel-rims. // KAvk_64.108 //
These [trees], with creeper-garlands expanding on the banks of the clear <s>Narmadā</s> —

children.text: śuśrāva nirjane kīrṇaṃ kinnaryāḥ karuṇaṃ svanam // KAvk_64.110 //
so 'bhyetya sadguṇādarśas tāṃ dadarśa mṛgīdṛśam // KAvk_64.111 //
khinnām iva vanabhrāntyā lakṣmīṃ hariṇalakṣmaṇaḥ // KAvk_64.113 //
sāṃrājye jagatāṃ yayā vijayate devo vilāsāyudhaḥ // KAvk_64.117 //
tāṃ pibantam ivābhyetya praṇamya prāha lubdhakaḥ // KAvk_64.118 //
tvam evāsyā guṇodāra bhartā bhuva ivocitaḥ // KAvk_64.120 //
gṛhītas tadvirahitā neyaṃ yāti vihāyasā // KAvk_64.121 //
rakṣyo maṇir ayaṃ nāsti datte 'smin saṃgamo 'nayā /
ity uktvāsmai dadau kanyāratnaṃ ratnaṃ ca lubdhakaḥ // KAvk_64.122 //
kinnarīṃ ratham āropya ratnair āpūrya lubdhakam /
sa hastināpuraṃ prāpya nivedya svakathāṃ pituḥ /
harṣād vismayinā tena vivāhe vihitotsavaḥ // KAvk_64.126 //
sukṛtair bhogyatāṃ yātāṃ mūrtām iva śaśiśriyam /
spṛṣṭā natamukhāmbhojā cakampe nalinīva sā // KAvk_64.128 //
vailakṣye 'pi sphuṭallakṣmīṃ tasyāḥ prītiṃ tatāna saḥ // KAvk_64.129 //
vivāda iva sotkampaṃ kaṅkaṇasvanayor abhūt // KAvk_64.131 //
ājagmatur vṛttikāmau dhanasya nṛpateḥ sabhām // KAvk_64.133 //
vidadhe madalekheva vidyā malinatām mukhe // KAvk_64.136 //
sadā saṃsadi mām eva nayaty eṣa vilakṣatām // KAvk_64.139 //
tasmād āśrayam evāsya śrīmūlam praharāmy aham // KAvk_64.141 //
yuktaḥ kartuṃ prayatno me mānamlāniṃ kathaṃ sahe // KAvk_64.142 //
nāsti tat pātakaṃ loke yan na kurvanti matsarāḥ // KAvk_64.143 //
kathaṃ paśyati sadvartma sa sadā vyathitāśayaḥ /
rāgaḥ pāpaṃ paramam adhikaṃ darpapāpaṃ tato 'pi
krodhāt pāpaṃ jagati na paraṃ duḥsahaṃ lobhapāpam /
yāvān eṣa vyasanini jane gaṇyate pāpavargaḥ
pāpāṃśasya spṛśati na tulāṃ so 'pi vidveṣasūteḥ // KAvk_64.145 //
tataḥ kadā cin meghākhyaṃ krūraṃ karvaṭavāsinam /
amātyānāṃ anumate kumāram idam abravīt // KAvk_64.147 //
kumāra gamyatāṃ tūrṇam ucchettuṃ tarasā ripum /
kramopapannaṃ sāṃrājyaṃ niḥśalyam idam astu te // KAvk_64.148 //
hate tava pratāpasya nirvighnāvaraṇā diśaḥ // KAvk_64.150 //
durbalaiḥ kiṃ hatair anyaiḥ sāmantair antavāsibhiḥ /
dṛptaḥ sa eva hantavyas tadvadhe sarvasiddhayaḥ // KAvk_64.151 //
tat tasya pauruṣakathāpatham eti śauryam // KAvk_64.152 //
jananīṃ svairam abhyetya praṇipatya jagāda saḥ // KAvk_64.154 //
dātavyaḥ sarvathā mātar nānyatra prāṇasaṃśayāt // KAvk_64.156 //
nikṣipya sa yayau tūrṇaṃ sainyācchāditadiṅmukhaḥ // KAvk_64.157 //

children.translated_text: On her hand, upon the fallen and jingling bracelet, by its looseness,
the stream of tears quickly created a garland-like pattern of pearls. (KAvk_64.160)

children.text: dveṣaḥ puṣpaśare sukhe vimukhatā dehe 'pi niḥsnehatā
children.translated_text: Hatred toward <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the flower-arrowed god), aversion to pleasure, detachment even from the body,
constant meditation focused on her husband, ceaseless chanting of his name as a <s>mantra</s>,

children.text: śayyā bhūmitalaṃ tathāpi sutanos tāpakṣatir nābhavan
children.translated_text: the bare ground as her bed — yet even so, the burning anguish of her son's absence did not cease;

children.text: nūnaṃ niścalalīnarāgamanasāṃ muktir na tīvravrataiḥ // KAvk_64.161 //
children.translated_text: surely for those whose minds are absorbed in steadfast passion, liberation does not come even through the most severe vows. (KAvk_64.161)
Reclining on a crystal couch, pale as <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood),

children.text: candralekheva sā tanvī jyotsnāmadhyagatā babhau // KAvk_64.162 //
children.translated_text: that slender woman shone like a crescent moon set amidst moonlight. (KAvk_64.162)
Then one day, the king, alarmed by a dream vision,

children.text: purohitaṃ samāhūya papraccha kapilaṃ rahaḥ // KAvk_64.163 //
children.translated_text: summoned the <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) <s>Kapila</s> and questioned him in private. (KAvk_64.163)

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ adya mayā svapne niruddhaṃ śatrubhiḥ puram /
children.translated_text: "Today I saw in a dream the city besieged by enemies,
encircled by my entrails, drawn out from my split-open belly. (KAvk_64.164)
Tell me, O great wise one, the fruit that this dream portends as its ripened consequence;

children.text: vicintaya śubhodarkām ucitāṃ ca pratikriyām // KAvk_64.165 //
children.translated_text: consider an appropriate counter-remedy that will lead to an auspicious outcome." (KAvk_64.165)

children.text: iti pṛṣṭaḥ kṣitīśena kṣaṇam antaḥ purohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus asked by the king, the <s>purohita</s> (priest), for a moment, inwardly,
feigning meditation with a pretense of devotion, contemplated his own design. (KAvk_64.166)
"This stratagem, long contemplated by me, has by good fortune been obtained —
for the destruction of the prince, so as to uproot <s>Puṣkara</s>'s refuge. (KAvk_64.167)

children.text: priyā manoharā jyeṣṭhaṃ jīvitaṃ tasya kinnarī /
children.translated_text: The beloved <s>kinnarī</s> <s>Manoharā</s> is the very life of that eldest son;

children.text: abhāve niyataṃ tasyā na sa jīvati duḥkhitaḥ // KAvk_64.168 //
children.translated_text: in her absence, he will surely not survive, consumed by grief." (KAvk_64.168)
Having thus deliberated, with feigned sorrow and dejection,
the <s>purohita</s>, who wished the king ill, slowly addressed the lord of the earth. (KAvk_64.169)
"This is a terrible dream, O lord, exceedingly heart-shaking;

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ spaṣṭaṃ phalaṃ tasya duḥsahaṃ katham ucyate // KAvk_64.170 //
children.translated_text: you have seen it clearly — how can its unbearable fruit be spoken? (KAvk_64.170)
For those who are devoted to their master and steadfast in their vows, who are not negligent regarding faults,

children.text: na karṇakaṭukaṃ vaktuṃ niṣedho 'sti hitaiṣiṇām // KAvk_64.171 //
children.translated_text: there is no prohibition for well-wishers against speaking what is harsh to the ear. (KAvk_64.171)

children.text: rājyāt bhraṃśaḥ śarīrād vā svapnasyāsya phalaṃ sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: Loss of kingdom or of the body — the fruit of this dream is evident;
a counter-remedy must be performed here without hesitation for your well-being. (KAvk_64.172)
In a sacrificial pool filled with the blood of sacrificial animals,

children.text: snātas tvaṃ mārjito viprair bhūriratnasuvarṇadaḥ // KAvk_64.173 //
children.translated_text: you should bathe, be purified by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and give abundant gems and gold. (KAvk_64.173)
Having offered the fat of a <s>kinnarī</s> into the fire, you shall attain welfare;

children.text: antaḥpure snuṣā te 'sti kinnarī na tu durlabhā // KAvk_64.174 //
children.translated_text: in the inner apartments, your daughter-in-law is a <s>kinnarī</s> — she is not hard to obtain." (KAvk_64.174)

children.text: iti tasya vacaḥ śrutvā krūraṃ pātakakūṇitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing his cruel words, the king recoiled in horror at the sin,
and, alarmed by the barbarous proposition, spoke to him thus. (KAvk_64.175)
"How can I undertake the slaughter of a woman for the sake of preserving my own life?

children.text: kinnarīvirahe 'vaśyaṃ na ca jīvati me sutaḥ // KAvk_64.176 //
children.translated_text: And if the <s>kinnarī</s> is taken away, my son will surely not survive." (KAvk_64.176)
When the king thus rejected his design,

children.text: taṃ pāpābhiniveśena punaḥ prāha purohitaḥ // KAvk_64.177 //
children.translated_text: the <s>purohita</s>, with evil insistence, spoke to him again. (KAvk_64.177)

children.text: aho rājan na jānīṣe dhīmān api janasthitim /
children.translated_text: "Alas, O king, wise though you are, you do not understand the way of the world;

children.text: trivargasādhanaṃ tyājyam na rājyaṃ na ca jīvitaṃ // KAvk_64.178 //
children.translated_text: the means to the three aims of life must not be abandoned — neither kingdom nor life itself. (KAvk_64.178)

children.text: arthā iva svajanamitrakalatraputrā naṣṭāḥ sthitasya puruṣasya punar bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Just as wealth, kinsmen, friends, wives, and sons return again for a man who remains alive though they are lost,

children.text: ucchvāsamātravirahe gatajīvitasya tatkālasaṃnihitam apy asad eva sarvam // KAvk_64.179 //
children.translated_text: so for one who has died, separated even for a single breath, everything present at that moment becomes as nothing. (KAvk_64.179)
For the sake of life, one's own country, beloved ones, and sons are abandoned;

children.text: jīvitād aparaṃ rājañ jīvaloke 'sti na priyam // KAvk_64.180 //
children.translated_text: O king, in the world of the living, nothing is dearer than life itself." (KAvk_64.180)
Thus, through greed for life, by his various arguments and illustrations, gradually

children.text: pratāritaḥ pāpaṃ rājā yuktam amanyata // KAvk_64.181 //
children.translated_text: the king was deceived and came to consider the sinful act appropriate. (KAvk_64.181)
Then, when the preparations for the sacrifice were well under way and the ritual rites had commenced,

children.text: kṛtāyāṃ puṣkariṇyāṃ ca pūrṇāyāṃ paśuśoṇitaiḥ // KAvk_64.182 //
children.translated_text: and the sacrificial pool had been made and filled with the blood of animals, (KAvk_64.182)
the queen, privately informed of the proceedings by the king himself,
grieving at her son's absence abroad and terrified of the sin, reflected thus. (KAvk_64.183)
"Alas, the king is utterly foolish — driven by the priest blinded by delusion
into this scheme of slaughtering the daughter-in-law, a monstrous sin! (KAvk_64.184)
Even when death's appointed limit cannot be averted by any effort,
fools desire to live by taking the lives of others! (KAvk_64.185)
If, greedy for life, the king kills even the daughter-in-law, innocent as a doe,

children.text: snuṣāpi hanyate rājñā tat kiṃ vakṣyāmy ahaṃ sutam // KAvk_64.186 //
children.translated_text: then what shall I say to my son? (KAvk_64.186)

children.text: mātas tvayeyaṃ vātsalyāt pālyā mama manoharā /
children.translated_text: 'Mother, out of affection, please protect my <s>Manoharā</s>' —

children.text: ity uktvā sudhanaḥ sūnur gato nikṣipya me vadhūm // KAvk_64.187 //
children.translated_text: having said this, my son <s>Sudhana</s> departed, entrusting his bride to me. (KAvk_64.187)

children.text: tasmāc cūḍāmaṇim mattaḥ prāpya vyomnā prayātu sā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, let her take the <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s> (crest-jewel) from me and fly through the sky;

children.text: bhaviṣyati tayā patyur jīvantyā saṃgamaḥ punaḥ // KAvk_64.188 //
children.translated_text: while she lives, there will be a reunion with her husband again." (KAvk_64.188)

children.text: iti saṃcintya sā gatvā sāśrunetrā snuṣāntikam /
children.translated_text: Having resolved thus, she went with tear-filled eyes to the daughter-in-law,

children.text: rājavṛttaṃ nivedyāsyai sotkampā punar abravīt // KAvk_64.189 //
children.translated_text: and having informed her of the king's deed, said again, trembling. (KAvk_64.189)

children.text: vatse cūḍāmaṇiṃ baddhvā gaccha tūrṇaṃ vihāyasā /
children.translated_text: "Dear child, binding the <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s> (crest-jewel) upon you, depart swiftly through the sky;

children.text: nṛpaḥ pāpapravṛtto 'yaṃ na sadācāram īkṣate // KAvk_64.190 //
children.translated_text: this king has turned to evil and does not regard righteous conduct. (KAvk_64.190)
You must go to the sacrificial ground and from there take to the aerial path;

children.text: anyathā tvām asau vetti gūḍhanyastāṃ mayā kva cit // KAvk_64.191 //
children.translated_text: otherwise he will think you have been secretly hidden by me somewhere." (KAvk_64.191)
Hearing these words, <s>Manoharā</s>, already grieving at her husband's absence abroad,

children.text: tatsaṃgamāya rakṣantī yatnāt priyataraṃ vapuḥ // KAvk_64.192 //
children.translated_text: carefully guarding her body, dearer still for the sake of reunion with him, (KAvk_64.192)

children.text: śvaśrvā dattaṃ samādāya baddhvā mūrdhni śikhāmaṇim /
children.translated_text: took the crest-jewel given by her mother-in-law, bound it upon her head,

children.text: nṛpāhūtā kratukṣetraṃ gatvā vyoma vyagāhata // KAvk_64.193 //
children.translated_text: and summoned by the king to the sacrificial ground, she went there and then ascended into the sky. (KAvk_64.193)

body.text:
rājan naitat tava samucitaṃ yat priyasyāpi sūnor
vadhyā patnī nijapadam iyaṃ svasti tubhyaṃ gatāham /
rakṣyaś cāsau pratihatadhṛtir madviyoge kumāras

children.text: tatrety uktvā tanutaratadidvibhramaiḥ sā jagāma // KAvk_64.194 // /
children.translated_text: having spoken thus there, she departed with the flashing movements of a slender lightning bolt. (KAvk_64.194)
When she had gone, the king became alarmed at the disruption of the sacrifice,

children.text: purohitas tam avadad deva mā saṃśayaṃ kṛthāḥ // KAvk_64.195 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>purohita</s> said to him, "Lord, have no doubt! (KAvk_64.195)

body.translated_text: "O king, this is not worthy of you — that the wife of your own dear son should be slain; I am going to my own abode; farewell to you! And that prince, his resolve shattered by separation from me, must be protected by you" —

children.translated_text: A <s>brahmarākṣasa</s> (brahmin-demon) named <s>Krūra</s> (the Cruel One) was summoned by my <s>mantras</s>;

children.text: nirvighnas te kratuḥ siddhaḥ sā hatā tena kinnarī // KAvk_64.196 //
children.translated_text: your sacrifice is accomplished without obstruction — that <s>kinnarī</s> was killed by him." (KAvk_64.196)

children.text: iti mithyāvacas tasya rājā satyam amanyata /
children.translated_text: The king believed the false words of the priest to be true;
the naive are made to dance by the trickery of deceitful ones, like puppet-figures on strings. (KAvk_64.197)
<s>Manoharā</s>, arriving at her father's house, overflowing with joy,

children.text: nyavedayat svavṛttāntaṃ vahantī vallabhaṃ hṛdi // KAvk_64.198 //
children.translated_text: reported all that had happened, carrying her beloved in her heart. (KAvk_64.198)
By her father's command, to remove the fragrance of mortal contact,

children.text: hemakumbhaśataiḥ snānaṃ pañcabhiḥ pratyahaṃ vyadhāt // KAvk_64.199 //
children.translated_text: she bathed daily with five hundred golden pitchers. (KAvk_64.199)
The mortal scent gradually diminished as she was washed;

children.text: sudhanasnehasaṃyogī na tu rāgo mṛgīdṛśaḥ // KAvk_64.200 //
children.translated_text: but the passion of the doe-eyed one, joined with love for <s>Sudhana</s>, did not fade. (KAvk_64.200)
She found no delight in the enjoyments of the celestial gardens;

children.text: anyatra baddharāgāṇāṃ ratir nānyatra dehinām // KAvk_64.201 //
children.translated_text: for those whose love is fixed on another, there is no pleasure elsewhere. (KAvk_64.201)
She, weary from separation from her beloved, once, traversing the sky,
went to that land at the edge of the forest near the abode of the <s>Nāgas</s>. (KAvk_64.202)
There, she approached the great sage, clad in bark garments, dwelling in the hermitage ground,
and spoke to him, her face bowed in salutation. (KAvk_64.203)
"It was by your direction to the hunter that my capture was brought about;

children.text: tvam eva brūhi bhagavan yadi yuktam idaṃ kṛtam // KAvk_64.204 //
children.translated_text: tell me yourself, O blessed one, whether what was done was right." (KAvk_64.204)
Hearing her words, the sage, his face slightly touched with shame,

children.text: tām uvāca munir mugdhe tavaiṣā bhavitavyatā // KAvk_64.205 //
children.translated_text: said to her, "O innocent one, this was your destiny. (KAvk_64.205)
Not knowing that he possessed an unfailing snare, I spoke;

children.text: upalabhya kathāṃ dhūrtas tvāṃ babandha sa lubdhakaḥ // KAvk_64.206 //
children.translated_text: and that cunning hunter, having learned the information, captured you. (KAvk_64.206)
We do not comprehend the crookedness of evil-souled ones with cruel hearts;
we are by nature straightforward, outspoken in truthful speech." (KAvk_64.207)

children.text: ity uktā muninā tanvī praṇayāt tam abhāṣata /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the sage, the slender woman spoke to him with affection:
"O blessed one, forgive this — the impetuous speech of a young girl. (KAvk_64.208)

children.text: idaṃ tu bhavatām agre yan mayā kiṃ cid ucyate /
children.translated_text: But this much I may say before you reverend ones —
this is a transgression of proper conduct easily found in women. (KAvk_64.209)
That even elders become objects of gossip when there is rashness —
that is the intolerance born of the flames of the fire of separation's anguish. (KAvk_64.210)
Those who are compassionate toward the afflicted, ready to rescue them from suffering,

children.text: kāryāntaraṅgāḥ prāyeṇa bhavanty anuciteṣv api // KAvk_64.211 //
children.translated_text: generally become deeply involved in matters, even in inappropriate ones. (KAvk_64.211)
I was freed from the snare by the hunter's idle talk —
Bound by the prince with the captivating noose of love,
that fortunate one named <s>Sudhana</s>, tormented by the fire of separation from me,

children.text: amunā yadi mārgeṇa sameṣyati tavāntikam // KAvk_64.213 //
children.translated_text: if he should come to your presence by this path,

children.text: tad idaṃ bhavatā vācyaṃ kāruṇyād vacasā mama /
children.translated_text: then, out of compassion, these words of mine should be spoken by you:
"I dwell in my father's house, joyless from the agony of separation from you.

children.text: utkaṇṭhām anukampāṃ vā sahajāṃ vā kṛtajñatām /
children.translated_text: Whether out of longing, or compassion, or innate gratitude,

children.text: dākṣiṇyaṃ vā puraskṛtya tūrṇam āgamyatām itaḥ // KAvk_64.215 //
children.translated_text: or courtesy — come here swiftly, putting any of these foremost."
The path to the <s>Kinnara</s> realm is difficult, beset with a hundred hardships,
and utterly impassable for mortals of meager valor, strength, and vitality.
At the edge of this <s>tapovana</s> (ascetic grove), there blazes a great herb called <s>Sudhā</s>;

children.text: dṛśyate haviṣā paktvā pātavyā sā svayaṃ tvayā // KAvk_64.217 //
children.translated_text: it can be seen when cooked with <s>havis</s> (clarified butter offering) — it must be drunk by you yourself.
By its power, having overcome hardship, accompanied by courage,
you shall reach my city by the path bright as the laughter of <s>Kailāsa</s>.
And this ring of mine, a token of recognition, should be given to him."

children.text: ity uktvā viṣamaṃ vartma kathayitvā krameṇa sā // KAvk_64.219 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, and having described the perilous path step by step, she
instructed him in the means to counteract obstacles through wondrous devices,
and departed, giving the ring, her life sustained only by the thread of hope.
Having heard from her the marvel of crossing the long distance,

children.text: aṅgulīyakam ādāya tad evācintayan muniḥ // KAvk_64.221 //
children.translated_text: the sage took the ring and pondered over that very matter.
Meanwhile, the prince, having conquered king <s>Megha</s>,
returned carrying the treasury, eager for the sight of his beloved.

body.text:
sa viveśa svanagarīṃ sāmantacchattramaṇḍalaiḥ /
phullaphenasmitasyābdheḥ kurvāṇaḥ saṃnibhaṃ nabhaḥ // KAvk_64.223 // snuṣāvaiśasavṛttāntakathanakleśakampitam /

children.text: athāntaḥpuram abhyetya janakaṃ praṇanāma saḥ // KAvk_64.224 //
children.translated_text: then, approaching the inner palace, he bowed before his father.

body.translated_text: He entered his own city, with the canopy-circles of his feudatories, making the sky resemble an ocean smiling with blossoming foam; trembling with the distress of narrating the events of the daughter-in-law's calamity,

children.translated_text: All the people with downcast faces, the festivities slain by the arrow of grief —

children.text: pitur antaḥpuraṃ dṛṣṭvā sa vipriyam aśaṅkata // KAvk_64.225 //
children.translated_text: seeing his father's inner palace thus, he apprehended some misfortune.

children.text: api jīvati sā tanvī virahārtā manoharā /
children.translated_text: "Does that slender one, <s>Manoharā</s>, afflicted by separation, still live?"

children.text: iti bruvāṇaṃ na yadā tam ūce kaś cid apriyam // KAvk_64.226 //
children.translated_text: When no one spoke anything unpleasant to him as he asked thus,

children.text: tadā jagāda jananī putra jīvati te priyā /
children.translated_text: then his mother said: "Son, your beloved is alive,

children.text: gatā cūḍāmaṇiṃ prāpya kiṃ tu jīvitasaṃśaye // KAvk_64.227 //
children.translated_text: but having obtained the <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s> (crest-jewel), she has departed — her very life now in doubt."

body.text:
iti śrutvaiva sahasā sa papāta mahītale /
kīrṇahāralatāṃ kurvan sāśrudhārām iva kṣitim // KAvk_64.228 // tuṣāraśīkarasmeraharicandanavāribhiḥ /

children.translated_text: he slowly regained consciousness and lamented, his voice choked with tears.

body.translated_text: Hearing this, he suddenly fell to the ground, making the earth appear as though it wore a scattered necklace-garland of tears; with waters of <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood) sprinkled by cool dewdrops,

children.translated_text: "The beauty of the moon without the sky! The nectar-bearer without the churning!
The jewel-pavilion obtained without effort! Where is she, that weapon of the flower-armed <s>Kāma</s>?
Restrained by my father's command, as I departed far, my eyes blocked by tears,

children.text: vihitā na dhṛtir mayā mṛgākṣyās tad ayaṃ me patitaḥ smarābhiśāpaḥ // KAvk_64.231 //
children.translated_text: I could not give comfort to that doe-eyed one — therefore this curse of <s>Smara</s> (Love) has fallen upon me.

children.text: dehi prativacaḥ subhru kva gatāsi manohare /
children.translated_text: Give me an answer, O beautiful-browed one! Where have you gone, <s>Manoharā</s>?

children.text: mayā pramādamūḍhena hariṇākṣī na rakṣitā // KAvk_64.232 //
children.translated_text: By me, deluded through negligence, that doe-eyed one was not protected.
Of this mortal world, which boasted the good fortune of union with you,

children.text: mameva martyalokasya tvadviyuktasya kā dyutiḥ // KAvk_64.233 //
children.translated_text: praised in the assembly of the gods — what splendor remains for me, now separated from you?"
Speaking thus, slowly, in the gardens that had witnessed his beloved's embrace,

children.text: udyāneṣu priyatamāṃ vicetuṃ svayam udyayau // KAvk_64.234 //
children.translated_text: he himself set out to search for his dearest one.
Having eluded his attendants, unnoticed in the night,

children.text: gatvā vanāntaṃ babhrāma sameṣu viṣameṣu ca // KAvk_64.235 //
children.translated_text: he went to the forest's edge and wandered over level and uneven ground.
Deluded by the great demon of intense passion,

children.text: unmatta iva papraccha cetanācetanān api // KAvk_64.236 //
children.translated_text: like a madman, he questioned both the sentient and the insentient.

body.text: brūhi sakhe śukaśāvaka sakhyuḥ prāṇasakhīṃ nikhilendumukhīṃ tām / taddaśanacchadarāgavibhāge bimbaphale 'stu sadā tava bhogaḥ // KAvk_64.237 //
body.translated_text: "Tell me, friend, young parrot, of my friend — that moon-faced beloved, the companion of my very life! In reward, may you always enjoy the <s>bimba</s> fruit, which shares the redness of her teeth's radiance!

children.translated_text: Ho, <s>haṃsa</s> (swan)! O white-winged one! Tell me, O you who shine as an ornament in the play of lotus ponds,
have you seen her anywhere — that lotus-faced one, dwelling in fragrance, surging with beauty?
She, upon whose full, upraised breasts a string of pearls rolls,

children.text: haṃsasyeva vibhāti romalatikā śaivālavallī cyutā // KAvk_64.238 //
children.translated_text: and whose line of body-hair appears like a strand of moss fallen from a swan."
As he thus lamented, driven by the force of intense affliction, stumbling even on level ground,

children.text: diśan prakāśaṃ dayayeva mārge śanair jagāhe gaganaṃ sitāṃśuḥ // KAvk_64.239 //
children.translated_text: the white-rayed moon slowly entered the sky, illuminating his path as if out of compassion.

children.text: śyāmāpater manmathabāndhavasya kāntaṃ sa dṛṣṭvāmbaracumbi bimbam /
children.translated_text: Seeing the lovely orb of the dark-complexioned one's kinsman, <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), touching the sky,

children.text: saṃdarśitaṃ sasmitam indumukhyā mene mukhaṃ vyomavimānaśrṅgāt // KAvk_64.240 //
children.translated_text: he imagined it to be the smiling face of his moon-faced beloved, displayed from the peak of a celestial chariot.
Mute, marked by a stain, flawed,

children.text: cireṇa niścitya śaśāṅkam eva papraccha gacchan naranāthasūnuḥ // KAvk_64.241 //
children.translated_text: without coquetry, devoid of laughter and grace — after a long while, ascertaining it to be indeed the moon, the prince continued on, asking:

children.text: api tvayā kāntisakhī sakhe khe tulyekṣaṇā lakṣmaṃrgasya dṛṣṭā /
children.translated_text: "O friend, have you seen in the sky my companion in beauty, she who is equal in gaze to the deer-marked one?
Your fame in the world was obtained through the connection of being compared to her face."

body.text: kathaṃ na kiṃ cit kathayaty ayaṃ me gatasya kāntākathanārthibhāvam / parārthasaṃpādanaśītalena kalāvatā kasya kṛto 'nurodhaḥ // KAvk_64.243 //
body.translated_text: "Why does this moon say nothing to me, who has come seeking news of my beloved? By one who is cool in accomplishing others' purposes and possesses skill — for whom has any regard been shown?"

children.text: api tvayā snigdhataḍitprakāśā ghanastanī kvāpi mayūra dṛṣṭā /
children.translated_text: "O peacock, have you seen somewhere her whose radiance is like tender lightning, whose breasts are like clouds?

children.text: tvadbarhabhārasya suhṛt sa yasyā vicitramālyaḥ kabarīkalāpaḥ // KAvk_64.244 //
children.translated_text: Her colorful flower-braided hair is a friend to the burden of your tail-feathers."

children.text: bhujaṃga kac cid bhavatā bhujaṃgī dṛṣṭā kva cit sā vararatnacūḍā /
children.translated_text: "O serpent, have you perchance seen that serpent-maiden somewhere, she of the splendid jeweled crest?

children.text: viṣacchaṭāḥ paśya yayā visṛṣṭā māṃ duḥsahe 'smin virahe dahanti // KAvk_64.245 //
children.translated_text: See — the rays of poison she has released burn me in this unbearable separation!"

children.text: sāraṅga sā raṅgavilāsinī kiṃ dṛṣṭā tvayā manmathapārthivasya /
children.translated_text: "O deer, have you seen that beauty who delights in the arena of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), the king?

children.text: yasyāḥ kaṭākṣotpalasaṃvibhāgair vibhānti manye gahane hariṇyaḥ // KAvk_64.246 //
children.translated_text: By the distribution of the side-glances from her lotus-eyes, I believe, the doe-deer in the dense forest shine with beauty."
"O tree, birthplace of graceful charms, have you seen her — the one with lips tender as new shoots,

children.text: līlāvilolā lalanā vanānte lateva dṛṣṭā stabakāvanaṃrā // KAvk_64.247 //
children.translated_text: a playfully swaying woman at the forest's edge, like a vine bending under flower-clusters?"

children.text: anena nūnaṃ vanakuñjareṇa sā rājarambhā parirambhalobhāt /
children.translated_text: "Surely by this forest elephant, out of longing to embrace her,

children.text: ākṛṣya nītā ghanasaṃnibhena saṃcchāditā vā śaśinaḥ kaleva // KAvk_64.248 //
children.translated_text: that royal plantain-maiden has been seized and carried away, or perhaps, like a digit of the moon, she has been concealed by the cloud-like one."
Thus, as he wandered through the forest bowers, raving in his madness,

children.text: śokād iva vivarṇenduvadanā rajanī yayau // KAvk_64.249 //
children.translated_text: the night passed, her moon-face pale as if from grief.
He came to the <s>tapovana</s> (ascetic grove) near the bank at the foot of the <s>Nāga</s>-dwelling,

children.text: śanaiḥ praviśya papraccha maharṣiṃ valkalāyanaṃ // KAvk_64.250 //
children.translated_text: and entering slowly, he questioned the great sage <s>Valkalāyana</s>:
"Her single braid dark as the smoke of <s>Madana's</s> (Love's) fire, swelling with the sighs of grief born of separation's anguish here,

children.text: api śamitaśaśāṅkoddāmasaundaryadarpā munivara hariṇākṣī kinnarī kāpi dṛṣṭā // KAvk_64.251 //
children.translated_text: has any <s>Kinnarī</s>, doe-eyed, her pride of surpassing beauty humbled beyond even the moon, been seen, O best of sages?"
Thus, hearing the words of the one separated from his beloved,

children.text: muniḥ śrutvā vacas tasya parijñāya tam abravīt // KAvk_64.252 //
children.translated_text: who had reached a state of madness, the sage, recognizing him, spoke:
"Be consoled; rest now. Let this torment be abandoned.

children.text: dṛṣṭā sā tava kalyāṇī mayā mānasacandrikā // KAvk_64.253 //
children.translated_text: That auspicious one of yours, the moonlight of your heart — she has been seen by me.
Like a doe separated from the herd, indifferent even to life,

children.text: pāśākṛṣṭeva kariṇī dhāryate sā tvadāśayā // KAvk_64.254 //
children.translated_text: like an elephant-cow dragged by a snare, she is sustained only by her hope in you.
Her lotus-face rests in her hand upon a bed of leaves,
her limbs wearied by heat, their outline drooping with trembling and exhaustion;
like steadfastness clinging to hope, her mind, distracted by separation from you,

children.text: tasyā naiva kva cid api manaḥ kiṃ tu viśrāntim eti // KAvk_64.255 //
children.translated_text: finds no rest anywhere whatsoever.
'I dwell in the palace of my father, <s>Druma</s>, king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>;

children.text: āgantavyaṃ tvayā tūrṇam iti tvāṃ saṃdideśa sā // KAvk_64.256 //
children.translated_text: you must come swiftly' — thus she instructed you through me.
She also described, step by step, the path to the <s>Kinnara</s> realm, which is impassable

children.text: agamye kinnarapure kramād vartma śaśaṃsa ca // KAvk_64.257 //
children.translated_text: even for those possessing valor, courage, strength, resourcefulness, steadfastness, and enthusiasm.

children.text: idaṃ ca tvatkṛte dattaṃ tayā ratnāṅgulīyakam /
children.translated_text: And this jeweled ring was given by her for your sake,

children.text: yasya snigdhaprabhābhyaṅgair diśo yānti piśaṅgatām // KAvk_64.258 //
children.translated_text: whose affectionate luster anoints the directions with a golden hue."
Having spoken these words that were a support of courage, bathed in the nectar of joy,

children.text: aṅgulīyaṃ dadau tasmai mārgaṃ cākathayan muniḥ // KAvk_64.259 //
children.translated_text: the sage gave him the ring and described the path to him.
By the path indicated by him, equipped with the means, the prince

children.text: dhīraḥ pracakrame gantuṃ dhanadādhyuṣitāṃ diśam // KAvk_64.260 //
children.translated_text: resolutely set forth to travel toward the direction inhabited by <s>Kubera</s> (the lord of wealth).

children.text: sa siddhāṃ ghṛtapākena sudhāṃ pītvā mahauṣadhim /
children.translated_text: Having drunk the <s>Sudhā</s>, the great herb, prepared by cooking in ghee,
and having acquired the glory of supernatural power and strength, he set out slowly, armed.
By his supernatural power, all provisions were readily at hand on the path.
all wealth became subject to those whose companions were [beings of pure] <s>sattva</s> (goodness). // KAvk_64.262 //
Then, crossing the <s>Himavat</s> (Himālayas), radiant with the playful laughter

children.text: himavantam atikramya kukūlādrim avāpa saḥ // KAvk_64.263 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Vidyādhara</s> women, he reached Mount <s>Kukūla</s>. // KAvk_64.263 //
There, having won over the leader of a monkey troop with offerings of fruit,

children.text: vāyuvegākhyam āruhya sa taṃ śailam alaṅghayat // KAvk_64.264 //
children.translated_text: and mounting the one named <s>Vāyuvega</s> (Wind-speed), he crossed over that mountain. // KAvk_64.264 //
Then he crossed over the mountain named <s>Ajapatha</s> (Goat-path),
having slain a terrible python, as if destroying an assemblage of obstacles with an arrow. // KAvk_64.265 //
Having subdued a shape-shifting <s>rākṣasī</s> (demoness) with the sounds of a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute),
and leaping over Mount <s>Kāmarūpa</s>, the beloved of the <s>Kinnarī</s> proceeded onward. // KAvk_64.266 //
The mighty one, with supreme daring, then climbed
Mount <s>Ekadhāra</s> (Single-edge), [its path marked] by weapon-spikes driven in by mace-blows. // KAvk_64.267 //
Then, climbing the even more terrible mountain called <s>Vajraka</s>,
he beheld a <s>rākṣasī</s> in the form of a vulture, hungry for flesh. // KAvk_64.268 //
Concealed by wrapping himself in a turned-over fresh deer-skin,

children.text: sa pādamūle tasyādres tasthau niścalavigrahaḥ // KAvk_64.269 //
children.translated_text: he stood motionless at the foot of that mountain. // KAvk_64.269 //
The night-roaming demoness in vulture-form, greedy for flesh, snatched him up
and placed him on the summit of the peak to devour him, [she being] of terrifying form. // KAvk_64.270 //

children.text: mṛgacarma samutsṛjya tāṃ nihatya sa vīryavān /
children.translated_text: Casting off the deer-skin and slaying her, the valorous one
reached the <s>Khādira</s> mountain, densely covered with impenetrable <s>khadira</s> (acacia) trees. // KAvk_64.271 //

body.text: praviśya tadguhāṃ lebhe śilāṃ vyasya mahauṣadhim / śītātapatamaḥsarparākṣasādibhayāpahām // KAvk_64.272 //
body.translated_text: Entering its cave, he pushed aside a rock and found a great healing herb, / which dispels the dangers of cold, heat, darkness, serpents, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and the like. // KAvk_64.272 //

children.translated_text: Reaching the two machine-mountains whose clashing together was life-destroying,

children.text: yantrakīlaṃ śarāgreṇa chittvā cakre viniścalau // KAvk_64.273 //
children.translated_text: he cut the machine-bolt with the tip of his arrow and rendered them motionless. // KAvk_64.273 //
By cutting the machine-bolts, he tore open the machine-gate,

children.text: chedanam yantracakraṃ ca yantrayuktau tathāyasau // KAvk_64.274 //
children.translated_text: as well as the cutting machine-wheel, and likewise the two iron [guardians] set by machine, // KAvk_64.274 //
two men delivering fierce blows, and the unbearable machine-rams,
and likewise the <s>makara</s>-demons with their terrible machine-teeth that crush. // KAvk_64.275 //
Leaping over a terrifyingly dark and deep cave-well,

children.text: tuṅgāṃ saritam uttīrya hatvā tatkūlarākṣasān // KAvk_64.276 //
children.translated_text: and crossing a lofty river, having slain the <s>rākṣasas</s> on its banks, // KAvk_64.276 //
and [crossing] the river called <s>Pataṅga</s>, whose waters were covered with venomous serpents,

children.text: rodinīṃ ca nadīṃ tīre yasyāḥ kinnaraceṭikāḥ // KAvk_64.277 //
children.translated_text: and the river named <s>Rodinī</s> (the Weeping), on whose banks <s>Kinnarī</s> attendants // KAvk_64.277 //
create obstacles for those whose minds are set on [crossing] it, with the sounds of weeping;
and likewise the one named <s>Hāsinī</s> (the Laughing), [which steals] the minds of those robbed of their wits by laughter, // KAvk_64.278 //
on whose sandbanks <s>Kinnarī</s> women cause ruin —

children.text: laṅghayitvāpagāś cānyā vetrāṃ prāpya nadīṃ tataḥ // KAvk_64.279 //
children.translated_text: having leapt over these and other rivers, he then reached the river <s>Vetrā</s> (Reed-river). // KAvk_64.279 //
Clinging to the reed-creepers on its bank, wishing to cross it,
he caught hold of a reed-vine on the far shore, driven by the wind. // KAvk_64.280 //
By means of that [vine], as if by an exceedingly long hope, he reached the far bank,
and beheld the <s>Kinnara</s> city with its gleaming crystal mansions. // KAvk_64.281 //

children.text: praviśya sa śanaiḥ prapya kāntāṃ kanakapadminīm /
children.translated_text: Entering slowly, he reached a beautiful golden lotus-pond,
and climbing a tree on its bank, he stood hidden among jeweled creepers. // KAvk_64.282 //
There he saw <s>Kinnarī</s> women carrying water in golden vessels,

children.text: hemakumbhair jalaṃ tatra nayantīḥ kinnarāṅganāḥ // KAvk_64.283 //
children.translated_text: [the water] yellowish-fragrant with heaps of lotus-pollen. // KAvk_64.283 //
Approaching one of them who was weary from lifting a pitcher,

children.text: hastālambena sāhāyyaṃ kṛtvā papraccha tārn śanaiḥ // KAvk_64.284 //
children.translated_text: he helped her by supporting [the pitcher with] his hand, and gently asked her: // KAvk_64.284 //

children.text: mātaḥ kasya kṛte toyaṃ idaṃ yatnena nīyate /
children.translated_text: ‘Mother, for whose sake is this water carried with such effort?

children.text: yadbhaktyā gaṇyate nāyaṃ bhavatībhiḥ pariśramaḥ // KAvk_64.285 //
children.translated_text: Through whose devotion is this toil not reckoned by you ladies?’ // KAvk_64.285 //

children.text: iti tena priyagirā sā pṛṣṭā tam abhāṣata /
children.translated_text: Thus asked by him with pleasing words, she spoke to him,
instantly becoming partial toward [him], who bore the choicest beauty and sweetness. // KAvk_64.286 //
‘To dispel the odor of mortal [contact], <s>Manoharā</s> (the Enchanting One) always bathes

children.text: pituḥ kinnararājasya girā snāti manoharā // KAvk_64.287 //
children.translated_text: in fragrant waters, by the command of her father, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>.’ // KAvk_64.287 //

children.text: tayeti kathitaṃ śrutvā sudhāsikta iva kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Having heard what she said, as if instantly sprinkled with nectar,
he tossed into the golden pitcher his ring, which she [<s>Manoharā</s>] would recognize. // KAvk_64.288 //

children.text: snāntyās tatas tad abhihāri manoharāyāḥ kumbhāt papāta kucakumbhayuge 'ṅgulīyam /
children.translated_text: Then, as <s>Manoharā</s> bathed, the captivating ring fell from the pitcher onto the twin pitcher-like swelling of her breasts,
whose gem-ray-lines, glittering with radiance, instantly attained comparison with the beauty of nail-scratches. // KAvk_64.289 //
Then, recognizing the jeweled ring as though it were the embodiment
of her own love, intimate with the story of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love),

children.text: sā kāntam āgatam avetya kutas tvayedaṃ
children.translated_text: she, realizing that her beloved had come, said to the maidservant,

children.text: saṃprāptam ity avadad ucchaliteva dāsīm // KAvk_64.290 //
children.translated_text: as if overflowing [with joy]: ‘From where did you obtain this?’ // KAvk_64.290 //

children.text: tatas tām avadad dāsī devi puṣkariṇītaṭe /
children.translated_text: Then the maidservant said: ‘O goddess, on the bank of the lotus-pond

children.text: sthitaḥ ko 'pi yuvā kāntaḥ pratyakṣa iva manmathaḥ // KAvk_64.291 //
children.translated_text: stands a certain handsome youth, like <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) incarnate. // KAvk_64.291 //
This ring was placed by him into this golden pitcher;
its radiance, enclosed within, gives the water the beauty of saffron.’ // KAvk_64.292 //

children.text: iti tadvacanaṃ tanvī priyaṃ śrutvā manoharā /
children.translated_text: Hearing these pleasing words from her, the slender <s>Manoharā</s>,

children.text: niścitya dayitaṃ prāptam ānināya tayaiva tam // KAvk_64.293 //
children.translated_text: having ascertained that her beloved had arrived, brought him [to her] by means of that very [maidservant]. // KAvk_64.293 //
Having hidden her beloved in a most secluded garden-pavilion through [the maidservant],
<s>Manoharā</s> went and beheld him, like <s>Kumudvatī</s> (the night-lotus) [beholding] the moon. // KAvk_64.294 //
Through their mutual gazing in confusion, through the expression of the anguish of separation,

children.text: tayoḥ praharṣānubhavena lebhe śobhām aśeṣāṅgavatīm anaṅgaḥ // KAvk_64.295 //
children.translated_text: and through the experience of their delight, <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love) attained a beauty endowed with all its limbs. // KAvk_64.295 //

children.text: yad yat kiṃ cid virahasamaye cintayābhyastam antar
children.translated_text: Whatever had been inwardly rehearsed in thought during the time of separation,
whatever had been taught by <s>Manmatha</s>, the friend of ardent passion,

children.text: yad yat premṇaḥ sadṛśam ucitaṃ yad yad autsukyarāśes
children.translated_text: whatever was fitting and appropriate to love, whatever belonged to the heap of eagerness —

children.text: tat tat sarvaṃ praṇayasubhagaṃ dampatī cakratus tau // KAvk_64.296 //
children.translated_text: all of that the couple performed, beautiful with affection. // KAvk_64.296 //
Then <s>Manoharā</s>, ashamed of the concealed affair,
having confessed, showed her parents her husband, the earthly <s>Manobhava</s> (love incarnate). // KAvk_64.297 //
Then the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>, his lower lip trembling with anger,
spoke, avoiding the sight of his daughter’s husband: // KAvk_64.298 //
‘Alas! Fallen by fate into folly toward an unworthy person,

children.text: na vimuñcasi durvṛtte kṣālyamānāpi raktatām // KAvk_64.299 //
children.translated_text: you do not abandon your attachment even when being washed [of it], O wicked girl! // KAvk_64.299 //
Your youth, your beauty worthy of the desire of celestials —

children.text: bata prayātam etat te martyasnehena śocyatāṃ // KAvk_64.300 //
children.translated_text: alas, all this has gone to pitiable ruin through love for a mortal! // KAvk_64.300 //
Born of a lofty lineage, overflowing with full youth,

children.text: nimnage kṣobhavibhraṣṭā yātāsi sutarām adhaḥ // KAvk_64.301 //
children.translated_text: like a river thrown from its course by a flood, you have sunk exceedingly low! // KAvk_64.301 //
Causing distress to the learned, bringing shame upon the family,

children.text: malinā khalavidyeva saṃmatāsi na kasya cit // KAvk_64.302 //
children.translated_text: you are esteemed by no one, like a defiled and tainted dark art! // KAvk_64.302 //

children.text: rūpamātreṇa tuṣṭā tvaṃ yadi martyavaśaṃ gatā /
children.translated_text: If you, satisfied by mere form, have fallen under the power of a mortal,

children.text: tat kiṃ na ramase hemanirmāṇapuruṣatviṣā // KAvk_64.303 //
children.translated_text: then why do you not delight in the beauty of a man made of gold? // KAvk_64.303 //
The beauty of a man of handsome form but devoid of power and virtue
is [merely] wall-painting, like [the beauty of] a man in a picture. // KAvk_64.304 //
Your husband deserves death, O wicked one! Ashamed of this low alliance,

children.text: mukhaṃ draṣṭuṃ na śaknomi tvadyācñāptadivaukasām // KAvk_64.305 //
children.translated_text: I cannot bear to look upon the faces of the celestials won by your supplication. // KAvk_64.305 //
Truly, a daughter, like old age to the body,

children.text: jareva kila kāyasya kanyā saṃkocakāriṇī // KAvk_64.306 //
children.translated_text: causes contraction [of pride] in a family, even one endowed with effort and rising glory. // KAvk_64.306 //’

children.text: iti sā bhartsitā pitrā tam uvāca natānanā /
children.translated_text: Thus rebuked by her father, she spoke to him with downcast face,
making a stringless necklace upon her breasts with drops of tears: // KAvk_64.307 //

children.text: kopād anucitaṃ tāta naitan māṃ vaktum arhasi /
children.translated_text: ‘Father, it is not fitting for you to say such improper things to me in anger!

children.text: na śrūyante prabhāveṇa kiṃ narāḥ kinnarādhikāḥ // KAvk_64.308 //
children.translated_text: Are not men heard of who are superior to <s>Kinnaras</s> in prowess? // KAvk_64.308 //

children.text: garuḍasyāpi durlaṅghyām imām ullaṅghya yaḥ kṣitim /
children.translated_text: He who has crossed this land, impassable even for <s>Garuḍa</s>,

children.text: prabhāvabhūmir āyāti manuṣyaḥ sa kathaṃ bhavet // KAvk_64.309 //
children.translated_text: and arrives as a ground of power — how could such a one be a mere mortal? // KAvk_64.309 //
The form of embodied beings accords with their inner qualities;

children.text: karoty ānanda saṃvādaṃ dyutir eva himatviṣaḥ // KAvk_64.310 //
children.translated_text: it is radiance alone that proclaims the agreement of the moon [with its nature of] delight. // KAvk_64.310 //

children.text: jātyā kiṃ kriyate tāta svabhāvānuguṇā guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: Of what use is birth, father? Virtues conform to one’s own nature!
The full moon drips nectar, though it is the sibling of <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison). // KAvk_64.311 //

children.text: bhavanty antarguṇāḥ ke cic channadoṣās tathāpare /
children.translated_text: Some have inner virtues; others have hidden faults.

children.text: aparīkṣya na kartavyā maṇīnāṃ mūlyalaṅghanā // KAvk_64.312 //
children.translated_text: One should not undervalue gems without examination.’ // KAvk_64.312 //

children.text: śrutvaitat kinnarapatis tat tatheti vicintya ca /
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the king of the <s>Kinnaras</s>, reflecting ‘So be it,’
summoned his son-in-law and spoke, wishing to test his virtues: // KAvk_64.313 //

children.text: tvayā kāntyā jitās tāvad ete kinnaradārakāḥ /
children.translated_text: ‘You have indeed conquered these <s>Kinnara</s> youths by your beauty.
But having demonstrated your power, you will deserve a divine alliance. // KAvk_64.314 //
Uproot this vast field of reeds in an instant, make it reed-free,

children.text: vyuptam anyūnam uccitya punar dehi tilādhakam // KAvk_64.315 //
children.translated_text: and then sow it; harvest it without deficit, and give back an <s>āḍhaka</s> (measure) of sesame.’ // KAvk_64.315 //
Show your firm skill in archery — hitting distant targets and the like.
Then this victory-banner, <s>Manoharā</s>, shall be yours.' // <s>KAvk</s> 64.316 //

children.text: ity aśakye 'pi kauṭilyāt preritas tena karmaṇi /
children.translated_text: Thus driven by [the king's] crookedness to a task [seemingly] impossible,

children.text: sarvaṃ kāntānurāgeṇa kumāraḥ kartum udyayau // KAvk_64.317 //
children.translated_text: the prince, out of love for his beloved, undertook to accomplish everything. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.317 //
Knowing him to be engaged in a task whose fruit was the deceptive toil of false trials,

children.text: taṃ vijñāya sahasrākṣaḥ pakṣapātād acintayat // KAvk_64.318 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> (<s>Indra</s>, the Thousand-eyed), out of partiality, reflected: // <s>KAvk</s> 64.318 //
'What! This prince, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Auspicious Aeon),
has been assigned by the <s>Kinnara</s>-king to a fruitless labor of hardship! // <s>KAvk</s> 64.319 //
I must render assistance to him in this arduous trial.'

children.text: iti saṃcintya śakro 'sya karmaniṣpattim ādadhe // KAvk_64.320 //
children.translated_text: Having thus resolved, <s>Śakra</s> set about accomplishing the task [for him]. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.320 //
By <s>Yakṣas</s> in the form of boars, dispatched by <s>Śatakratu</s> (<s>Indra</s>),

children.text: utpāṭite śaravane same vyuptaṃ tilādhakam // KAvk_64.321 //
children.translated_text: the arrow-grove was uprooted, and on the level ground a measure of sesame was sown. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.321 //
Gathered and collected by ants created by <s>Śakra</s>,
the prince presented [the sesame] to the astonished <s>Kinnara</s>-king. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.322 //
He then pierced seven golden pillars and seven palm trees,
fitted with boar-wheel mechanisms, with sharp-feathered arrows, mighty with strength, // <s>KAvk</s> 64.323 //
and displayed his skill in weapons, martial arts, crafts, and strength,

children.text: yayāsya petur mukuṭe divyāḥ kusumavṛṣṭayaḥ // KAvk_64.324 //
children.translated_text: whereupon divine showers of flowers fell upon his crown. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.324 //
Though astonished by his power, the <s>Kinnara</s> king

children.text: punas tadvañcanāyaiva tāṃ tāṃ yuktim acintayat // KAvk_64.325 //
children.translated_text: devised scheme after scheme to deceive him further. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.325 //

children.text: dadhati vipulāścarye maunaṃ hasanti satāṃ stutau
children.translated_text: Those who are hostile-minded maintain silence at great wonders, laugh at the praise of the virtuous,
become gloomy-faced at the rise of another's fame and resort to quarreling;

children.text: api guṇaśatair nārādhyante viruddhadhiyaḥ paraṃ paraparibhavakṣobhārambhasthirābhiniveśinaḥ // KAvk_64.326 //
children.translated_text: they are not propitiated even by a hundred virtues — firmly resolved only upon the aggression of humiliating others. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.326 //

children.text: sa tam ūce prabhāvo 'yaṃ divyaḥ prakaṭitas tvayā /
children.translated_text: He said to him: 'This divine power you have displayed.
Now you should demonstrate the excellence of your wisdom. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.327 //
Among <s>kinnarīs</s> of identical color and form,

children.text: kinnarīṇāṃ sthitāṃ madhye gṛhāṇa nijavallabhām // KAvk_64.328 //
children.translated_text: wearing the same ornaments and garments — seize your own beloved who stands among them.' // <s>KAvk</s> 64.328 //

children.text: ity uktas tena sa punaḥ kinnarīśatapañcakam /
children.translated_text: Thus told by him, [the prince] then beheld five hundred <s>kinnarīs</s>
of identical color, age, and dress, standing calmly before him. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.329 //

children.text: tāsāṃ madhye parijñāya sa jagrāha manoharām /
children.translated_text: Recognizing her among them, he seized <s>Manoharā</s>,
as a bee [finds] a mango-vine hidden in a thicket of creepers. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.330 //

children.text: devo 'yam iti niścitya tatas taṃ kinnareśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Concluding, 'This is a divine being,' the <s>Kinnara</s>-lord thereupon,

children.text: tuṣṭas tasmai dadau divyaratnaiḥ saha manoharām // KAvk_64.331 //
children.translated_text: pleased, gave him <s>Manoharā</s> along with divine jewels. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.331 //
Honored with splendid enjoyments and riches, respectfully,

children.text: jāyāsakhas tam āmantrya kumāraḥ svapuraṃ yayau // KAvk_64.332 //
children.translated_text: the prince, accompanied by his wife, took leave of him and returned to his own city. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.332 //
Seeing his son returned, with <s>Manoharā</s> at the fore, the king
shone like the nectar-ocean at the sight of the full moon. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.333 //

children.text: putraṃ tataś caritacandrasitātapatre rājye 'bhiṣicya paritāpaharaṃ prajānāṃ /
children.translated_text: Then, having consecrated his son in the kingdom under the moonlight-white parasol of his deeds, [a kingship] that removed the suffering of the people,

children.text: saṃtoṣaśītalavivekasukhābhirāmāṃ chāyām asevata nṛpaḥ praśamadrumasya // KAvk_64.334 //
children.translated_text: the king enjoyed the shade of the tree of tranquility — delightful with the coolness of contentment and the happiness of discernment. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.334 //

body.text: prāptābhiṣekaṃ sudhanam prabhāte taṃ saptaratnāni pṛthupratāpam / navaprabhāvaprabhubhāvabhītyā sevānivāsārtham ivopajagmuḥ // KAvk_64.335 //
body.translated_text: Upon <s>Sudhana</s>'s consecration, in the morning, the seven treasures [of a <s>Cakravartin</s>], [drawn] by the awe of his newly-manifest sovereign power, approached him as if for the purpose of rendering service. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.335 //

body.text: sa bodhisattvaḥ sudhano 'ham eva yaśodharā sāpi manoharābhūt

children.translated_text: The agony of the fire of grief at separation from her — all that I endured because of attachment to desire. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.336 //

body.translated_text: That <s>Bodhisattva Sudhana</s> was I myself; and <s>Yaśodharā</s> was indeed that <s>Manoharā</s>.

body.text:
tasmāt kāmaḥ kamalavadanānetraparyantavāsī
varjyaḥ sadbhiḥ śamaṃrgavadhūbandhakeliḥ kirātaḥ / sphūrjatpuṣpaprasarajarajaḥpuñjahālāhalāgrair

children.text: lokaḥ śokavyasanaviśikhair mohanair yena viddhaḥ // KAvk_64.337 //
children.translated_text: is pierced with deluding shafts of grief and calamity. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.337 //

body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Kāma</s> (Desire), who dwells at the corners of lotus-faced eyes, should be shunned by the good — that hunter who plays at binding the doe of tranquility; by whom the world, with the poison-tipped arrows of intoxicating pollen-clouds of sprouting flowers,

children.text: iti bhikṣugaṇaḥ svayaṃ jinena svakathāṃ tāṃ viniveditāṃ niśamya /
children.translated_text: Thus the assembly of monks, hearing from the <s>Jina</s> (the Victorious One) himself this story told about his own [past life],

children.text: sarasaṃ pṛthumūlam eva mene śataśākhasya manobhavam bhavasya // KAvk_64.338 //
children.translated_text: came to regard the tree of worldly existence (<s>bhava</s>), whose deep root is desire (<s>manobhava</s>), as having a hundred branches, juicy [yet poisonous]. // <s>KAvk</s> 64.338 //

body.text: iti kṣemendraviracitāyāṃ bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatāyāṃ sudhanakinnaryavadānaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭitamaḥ pallavaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā</s> composed by <s>Kṣemendra</s>, the <s>Sudhanakinnaryavadāna</s> is the sixty-fourth branch (<s>pallava</s>).
